module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1060

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1060](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1060)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Asymptotics Finset Filter Real
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos1060

/-- The conjecture is about the function $f(n)$ which counts the number of solutions to
$k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. The first bound is that $f(n)$ grows slower
than any power of $n^(\frac{1}{\log\log n})$. The second bound is that $f(n)$ is at most a power of
$\log n$.
-/

@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1060.parts.i :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℝ,
      h =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ 1 / log (log n)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ h n := by sorry

/-- Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1060.parts.ii :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), (fun n ↦ (#{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ log n ^ C) := by sorry

end Erdos1060

reformulations.difference: The source writes f(n) ≤ n^{o(1/log log n)}. Lean expresses this using an existential exponent function h, a little-o condition on h, and an eventual bound. It counts solutions in {0,…,n} rather than over unrestricted positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n>0, any solution has k>0 and σ(k)≥1, hence k≤kσ(k)=n, so the finite counting range is exact. The existential-exponent formulation is equivalent to: for every ε>0, eventually f(n)≤n^{ε/log log n}. Forward, use the little-o bound on h and monotonicity of real powers for n>1. Conversely, set h(n)=log(max(1,f(n)))/log n; the ε-bounds imply h=o(1/log log n), and n^{h(n)}=max(1,f(n)) for n>1. Both the counting identity and the asymptotic equivalence were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for f(n) ≤ (log n)^{O(1)}. Lean uses ∃ C : ℝ, f =O((log n)^C), allowing a separate multiplicative constant and not explicitly requiring C>0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These bounds are equivalent. If f(n)≤K(log n)^C eventually, then once log n≥max(K,1), f(n)≤(log n)^{C+1}≤(log n)^{max(C+1,1)}, with a positive constant exponent. Conversely, an eventual bound by a fixed power gives the stated big-O relation with multiplicative constant 1. A Lean proof establishes this equivalence for every nonnegative real-valued sequence and specializes it to the file's counting function.

review.notes:
Both declarations match the cited mathematical problem. The σ notation, casts, real powers, logarithms, finite-set cardinalities, and atTop filters have the intended meanings. The exceptional values σ(0)=0 and log(0)=log(1)=0 affect only initial inputs, not either asymptotic statement. Small cases were tested, including f(336)=2, and the counting function was proved to have positive values arbitrarily far out. The consolidated checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully; the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. The reviewed file remains unchanged.

Access limitation: the live problem page and linked forum/OEIS endpoints were inaccessible. The problem text and remarks were read from the June 5, 2026 archive snapshot, which records a September 28, 2025 last edit. The current linked problem database still records problem 1060 as open, agreeing with both category tags.
